description: Timestretch by repeating 'wavecycles': each wavecycle (or group of cyclecnt wavecycles) is played multiplier times in a row, stretching the sound and making it granular. Duration model verified on tone and noise inputs at multipliers 2–4 (worst error 0.23%); the model assumes skipcycles is 0. Mono only.
musical_use: Produces long, grainy, audibly stretched sounds — the wavecycle-repetition cousin of granular time-stretch, with a raw, distorted character. The striking trick is crossing the pitch-perception boundary: on noisy sources, raising cyclecnt groups enough identical repetitions together that each group reads as a pitch, turning noise into a string of pitch beads of arbitrary timbre; with cyclecnt around 128 you can get a slowish random melody. Time-varying multiplier (breakpoint file) gives accelerating/decelerating stretch.

multiplier.description: Number of times each wavecycle (group) repeats (integer; CDP-enforced range 2–32767 — the binary rejects 1 with 'Value (1.000000) out of range (2.000000 to 32767.000000)'). Output duration is roughly indur * multiplier. May vary over time (banner-confirmed, empirically verified).

cyclecnt.description: Number of wavecycles in each repeated group (integer; CDP-enforced range 1–32767; CDP's internal default is 1). Larger groups increase granularity and, on noisy sources, push the output across the pitch-perception boundary. May vary over time (banner-confirmed, empirically verified). Leaves the duration model essentially unchanged (0.45% error observed at cyclecnt 4).

skipcycles.description: Number of wavecycles to skip at the start of the file (integer; CDP-enforced range 0–32767; CDP's internal default is 0). Skipped material is dropped from the output entirely, so nonzero values make the duration model over-predict (see known_issues). Scalar only — a breakpoint file is refused.

examples.description: Stretch a source to three times its length with raw wavecycle repetition.
examples.expected_use: Grainy, obviously-stretched version of the source for texture beds.

examples.description: Turn a noisy source into a string of pitch beads.
examples.expected_use: Cross the pitch-perception boundary: each repeated group of 64 wavecycles reads as a pitch of arbitrary timbre.

known_issues: skipcycles removes the skipped wavecycles from the output rather than passing them through (verified: skipping 100 cycles of a 440 Hz tone shortened the output by ~2 x 100/440 s at multiplier 2). The duration model 'indur * multiplier' therefore over-predicts when skipcycles > 0; the shortfall is content-dependent (cycles, not seconds) and cannot be modelled statically.
skipcycles rejects breakpoint files: 'ERROR: Cannot read parameter 3 [sk.brk]: brkpnt_files not permitted.'
Mono only: a stereo input is refused with 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' (exit 255).
